hunks.baseline: That day, everything was different from usual.
hunks.sol: That day, everything was different.

hunks.baseline: The streets, where laughter and music never seemed to stop, were quiet. The clouds that had yet to clear cast shadows over everyone’s heads, and the canals, swollen by unprecedented rainfall, churned uneasily as if reflecting the state of things.

hunks.baseline: At the end of it all, and at its center, stood the imperial palace.
hunks.sol: At the end of those streets, and at their center, stood the imperial palace.

hunks.sol: It was the dim hour before dawn. Even when the massive iron gates began to open with a heavy metallic groan, no one thought anything strange was happening.

hunks.baseline: The imperial palace gates always closed at the hour of the Rat and opened at the hour of the Rabbit.

hunks.sol: But the dazzling light that appeared between the slowly opening gates was proof that this day would not begin like any other.

hunks.sol: The thousand riders shot forward like a single arrow, crossing the main road before the palace in the blink of an eye. At a hand signal from their commander, they scattered in every direction.

hunks.sol: The people who had started their day early watched in a daze. But when they saw the notices left behind by the golden tide that had swept through the Imperial Capital, they understood.

hunks.sol: A man in a worn bamboo hat pulled low over his face muttered the question on everyone’s mind.

hunks.sol: “The people’s will is Heaven’s will, and Heaven’s will is the people’s. Why, then, has the Emperor turned his back on Heaven and his people?”

hunks.sol: His voice rang clearly through the crowd, which had fallen silent.

hunks.baseline: The invisible air pressed down on them, heavy and still.
hunks.sol: The air seemed to press down on them.

hunks.sol: “Um, sir. Forgive me for interrupting, but could I ask you one thing?”
